how: Scenario 3, point 6. With `max_iterations` 4, iterations 0 to 3 of each loop run; iteration 4 would pass the limit: fault `LC8001`, with the iteration of the loop itself, 4 (cli.md 6.2 and 6.6, commands.md 7). Both loops end their iteration 3 at 400 ms, when their waits end; at that time the nodes of loop `n_a` come first in the global order (spec 8: its line, 20, comes before that of `n_b`, 34, in the canonical order, 5.2), so `n_a` reaches the limit first, at 400 ms, before any node of `n_b` runs. The loop is named by its first output (commands.md 8); it is in no loop, so `fault.loops` is empty, and its statement starts at line 20, column 5 of two_benches.lcf. The run stops like an abort (spec 8.2): no output, both sessions released by the runtime. The answers come from `python tests/acceptance/runs/noise.py 1 230 0.05 N` for SIM::DMM0 and `noise.py 2 12 0.01 N` for SIM::DMM1 (libs/visa/simulation.md, sections 3 and 4), one reading at the start of each iteration k, at 100k ms (no latency), then a wait of 100 ms. So each instrument saw 4 commands, at 0, 100, 200 and 300 ms.
